chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān and Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and he said: You begin with your hands, then wash your private part, then pour water over your head three times, then pour over the rest of your body two times. So whatever the water has flowed over has become tahir (ritually pure).

key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, over which water is poured three times
key_terms.سَائِرِ جَسَدِكَ: the rest of your body after the head
key_terms.طَهُرَ: has become ritually pure after water has flowed over it
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after the state of janabah
key_terms.فَرْجَكَ: your private part, washed before the rest of the ghusl
key_terms.كَفَّيْكَ: your two hands, which are to be washed first

ai.seo_question: How should ghusl of janabah be performed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the procedure of ghusl for janabah, beginning with washing the hands and private part, then pouring water over the head and the rest of the body. It indicates the ordered performance of the ghusl and affirms that whatever water reaches becomes tahir (ritually pure).
